forbidden_claim: CMD is soil-borne or persists in the soil as its normal transmission mechanism.
reason: Contradicted by source evidence describing whitefly transmission and infected planting material.

forbidden_claim: 1 m x 1 m cassava produces 25,000 plants per hectare.
reason: Arithmetic contradiction: 10,000 m2 / 1 m2 per planting position = 10,000.

forbidden_claim: CBSD is a disease of leaf veins only or only affects leaves.
reason: CBSD includes characteristic and economically destructive root symptoms.

forbidden_claim: Cassava cuttings must be cut above the nodes.
reason: Unsupported by Nigerian agronomy. The rule is simply clean cuts with sharp tools that preserve nodes.

forbidden_claim: Yam spacing is always 2 m x 2 m.
reason: Unsupported by any authoritative Nigerian source. 1 m x 1 m is standard for ware yam.

forbidden_claim: 1 m x 1 m is the universal spacing for all yams.
reason: False. Seed yam and minisett techniques require much closer spacing (e.g., 25 cm x 100 cm).

forbidden_claim: Yam must always be planted on mounds.
reason: False. Ridges are highly recommended for mechanization and minisetts, and flat beds are viable on deep, sandy soils.

forbidden_claim: Fertilizers or fungicides cure Yam Mosaic Virus, Cassava Mosaic Disease, or Cassava Brown Streak Disease.
reason: Biologically impossible. Fertilizers and fungicides do not cure viral infections.

forbidden_claim: Yam nematode damage will always be visible on the leaves as wilting or yellowing.
reason: Contradicts pathology. Scutellonema bradys destroys tubers with zero above-ground foliar symptoms.

forbidden_claim: Crop rotation immediately removes all nematodes from the field.
reason: Nematodes have wide host ranges (including weeds) and populations only decline gradually over extended periods.

forbidden_claim: ARIS can check live weather, access live market prices, or analyze uploaded photographs.
reason: Hardware/deployment constraints. The offline model has no internet access or computer vision capabilities.

forbidden_claim: Fertilizer cures or controls Fall Armyworm (FAW).
reason: False. Fertilizer improves plant vigor and resilience, but it has no insecticidal properties and cannot kill FAW.

forbidden_claim: Fertilizer cures Maize Streak Virus (MSV).
reason: False. MSV is a viral infection. Fertilizers provide soil nutrition and cannot neutralize plant viruses.

forbidden_claim: Striga can be permanently eradicated from a field in a single growing season.
reason: False. Striga produces thousands of long-lived seeds in the soil; management requires multi-year integrated approaches (rotation, tolerant varieties).

forbidden_claim: Maize Streak Virus is transmitted by whiteflies.
reason: Vector confusion. MSV is transmitted by Cicadulina leafhoppers. (Whiteflies transmit Cassava Mosaic Disease).

forbidden_claim: Aflasafe is a chemical fungicide that kills all Aspergillus fungi.
reason: False. Aflasafe is a biological control agent containing live, atoxigenic (non-toxic) strains of Aspergillus flavus that crowd out toxic strains.

forbidden_claim: Visible mould is required for maize to be contaminated with aflatoxins.
reason: False. Aflatoxins are invisible chemical toxins produced by fungi; highly contaminated grain can appear visually clean.

forbidden_claim: Fertilizer cures Rice Yellow Mottle Virus (RYMV) or Rice Blast.
reason: False. Fertilizers provide soil nutrition and cannot cure viral infections or fungal diseases.

forbidden_claim: Rice Yellow Mottle Virus is transmitted by whiteflies.
reason: Vector confusion. RYMV is transmitted by beetles and mechanical contact. (Whiteflies transmit Cassava Mosaic Disease).

forbidden_claim: RYMV is transmitted through true rice seeds.
reason: False. RYMV is not seed-transmitted, though surface contamination on husks/debris can occur.

forbidden_claim: Upland rice requires permanent standing water or deep flooding.
reason: False. Upland rice is grown under rainfed conditions on dry, non-puddled soils.

forbidden_claim: The sawah system completely prevents rice blast infection.
reason: False. Sawah cultivation does not preclude rice blast infection if weather and pathogen pressure are favorable.

forbidden_claim: Fertilizer cures or eliminates Striga hermonthica parasitism.
reason: False. Nitrogen application suppresses Striga and improves host vigor, but it does not cure the parasitic infection or destroy the soil seed bank.

forbidden_claim: Fertilizer cures Sorghum Anthracnose.
reason: False. Anthracnose is a fungal disease requiring resistant varieties or fungicides. Fertilizers have no fungicidal properties.

forbidden_claim: Sorghum anthracnose only affects the leaves of the plant.
reason: False. Colletotrichum sublineolum infects all above-ground tissues, including midribs, stalks (causing red rot), panicles, and grain.

forbidden_claim: One season of crop rotation or hand-pulling completely eradicates Striga from an infested field.
reason: False. Striga seeds remain viable in soil for 15–20 years; eradication requires multi-year integrated management.

forbidden_claim: Cowpea requires heavy nitrogen fertilization for optimal growth and yield.
reason: False. Cowpea is a legume that fixes atmospheric nitrogen through root nodules; excessive N causes lush vegetative growth with poor grain yield. Phosphorus is the primary nutrient focus.

forbidden_claim: PICS hermetic storage bags require chemical insecticides placed inside the bag to kill weevils.
reason: False. PICS bags are specifically designed as an insecticide-free, hermetic storage method that kills pests via oxygen depletion.

forbidden_claim: Spraying insecticide once at planting time controls Maruca pod borer for the entire season.
reason: False. Maruca attacks reproductive structures (buds, flowers, pods). Spraying must be timed around flower-bud initiation and flowering/podding stages.

forbidden_claim: Chemical fertilizers cure insect pest attacks or internal bruchid infestations in cowpea grain.
reason: False. Fertilizers provide plant nutrition and have no pesticidal or curative properties against insects.

forbidden_claim: Bacterial wilt of tomato can be cured or treated with conventional agricultural fungicides.
reason: False. Bacterial wilt is caused by the bacterium Ralstonia solanacearum. Fungicides only target fungi and have no effect on bacteria.

forbidden_claim: Blossom-end rot is a fungal or bacterial plant disease that spreads between tomato plants.
reason: False. Blossom-end rot is a non-parasitic physiological disorder caused by localized calcium deficiency linked to irregular water stress.

forbidden_claim: Tuta absoluta can be permanently eradicated from a tomato field with a single pesticide spray.
reason: False. Tuta absoluta has multiple overlapping life stages and rapid resistance development, requiring rigorous Integrated Pest Management (IPM).

forbidden_claim: Chemical fertilizers or household home remedies cure bacterial wilt or viral leaf curl infections in tomatoes.
reason: False. Pathogens are systemic bacteria and viruses; fertilizers and home mixtures possess no curative or therapeutic properties against them.

forbidden_claim: Soybean requires heavy applications of chemical nitrogen fertilizer for high grain yields.
reason: False. Soybean is a legume that fixes its own nitrogen through symbiotic root nodulation with rhizobia; excessive nitrogen suppresses nodulation and wastes resources.

forbidden_claim: Soybean rust can be cured or controlled using agricultural insecticides.
reason: False. Soybean rust is a fungal disease caused by Phakopsora pachyrhizi. Insecticides target insects and have no fungicidal properties.

forbidden_claim: Soybean seeds should be planted deeply (e.g., 7 cm or deeper) like yams to reach deep soil moisture.
reason: False. Deep planting drastically reduces seedling vigor and causes emergence failure; recommended depth is strictly 2 to 5 cm.

forbidden_claim: Chemical fertilizers cure viral infections or insect pest infestations in soybean crops.
reason: False. Fertilizers provide essential soil nutrients and possess no antiviral or pesticidal properties.

forbidden_claim: Groundnut does not require calcium for pod filling and seed development.
reason: False. Calcium is vital for proper pod and seed formation in the podding zone; gypsum (calcium sulfate) application at pegging is a standard agronomic requirement to prevent empty pods ('pops').

forbidden_claim: Groundnut Rosette Disease is a soil-borne pathogen that persists in the soil between seasons.
reason: False. Rosette is a viral complex transmitted persistently by the aphid vector Aphis craccivora, not by soil persistence.

forbidden_claim: Chemical fertilizers, fungicides, or post-infection insecticides cure Groundnut Rosette Disease.
reason: False. Rosette is a systemic viral infection; once a plant is infected, no chemical input can cure it.

forbidden_claim: Groundnut seeds should be planted deeply (e.g., 7 cm or more) to ensure moisture access.
reason: False. Deep planting impairs seedling emergence, reduces vigor, and causes uneven stands; recommended depth is strictly 3 to 5 cm.

forbidden_claim: Pearl millet requires permanent irrigation or high-water flooding conditions similar to lowland rice production.
reason: False. Pearl millet is a drought-tolerant dryland crop adapted to semi-arid savanna zones and cannot tolerate waterlogging or permanent flooding.

forbidden_claim: Chemical fertilizers or NPK top-dressings cure pearl millet downy mildew (green-ear disease).
reason: False. Downy mildew is a systemic oomycete infection (Sclerospora graminicola). Fertilizers provide nutrition and possess no fungicidal properties.

forbidden_claim: Foliar or systemic pesticide sprays can 'cure' or reverse panicle tissue already destroyed by millet head miner larvae.
reason: False. Head miner larvae feed internally on developing florets and grains; chemicals cannot restore consumed or severed plant tissue.

forbidden_claim: Dry planting is generally recommended as a primary agronomic rule for pearl millet in rainfed environments.
reason: False. Dry planting is discouraged because unpredictable early rains can cause seed germination failure and death in the soil before crop establishment.

forbidden_claim: Sweet potato can be routinely propagated for commercial root production using whole or cut storage roots as the primary planting material.
reason: False. Standard sweet potato agronomy relies strictly on apical and middle vine cuttings, not storage roots.

forbidden_claim: Applying heavy nitrogen fertilizer increases sweet potato storage root yield.
reason: False. Potassium is the primary nutrient for root bulking; excessive nitrogen causes lush vegetative vine overgrowth at the expense of storage roots.

forbidden_claim: Irish potatoes can be successfully grown in hot lowland tropical rainforests without specialized heat-tolerant varieties.
reason: False. Irish potato requires cool highland temperatures (such as Plateau State altitudes) and fails under unadapted lowland heat.

forbidden_claim: Conventional agricultural fungicides cure bacterial soft rot or bacterial wilt in stored potato tubers.
reason: False. Soft rot and bacterial wilt are caused by bacteria (e.g., Pectobacterium, Ralstonia). Fungicides target fungi and oomycetes and have zero antibacterial efficacy.

forbidden_claim: Onion bulbs size up entirely from heavy applications of chemical nitrogen fertilizer.
reason: False. Potassium (K) and sulfur (S) are critical for proper bulb formation and scaling; excess nitrogen promotes unwanted vegetative leaf growth at the expense of bulb sizing.

forbidden_claim: Uncured onions or onions with green, wet necks can safely undergo long-term bulk storage for months.
reason: False. Uncured neck tissue provides a moist entry pathway for fungal and bacterial pathogens, causing rapid post-harvest soft rot and storage failure.

forbidden_claim: Purple blotch of onion can be successfully cured or controlled using agricultural insecticides.
reason: False. Purple blotch is a fungal disease caused by Alternaria porri. Insecticides target insects and have no antifungal efficacy.

forbidden_claim: Chemical fertilizers or fungicides cure systemic viral mosaic/mottle infections in pepper plants.
reason: False. Plant viruses are systemic pathogens; neither soil fertilizers nor foliar fungicides possess antiviral curative properties.

forbidden_claim: Farmers can safely wash and reuse empty pesticide containers for storing household drinking water or food.
reason: False. Residues remain trapped in plastic materials despite washing, posing extreme public health and poisoning risks.

forbidden_claim: Unregistered local chemical mixtures or homemade concoctions are safe to apply if they have a strong smell or sting the skin.
reason: False. NAFDAC regulations strictly prohibit the use of unregistered pesticides, and sensory traits do not indicate chemical safety or toxicity limits.

forbidden_claim: Seeds and chemical fertilizers can be safely mixed together directly in the planting hole.
reason: False. Direct contact causes thermal and chemical 'seed burn', severely impairing germination and seedling vigor.

forbidden_claim: Foliar fungicides or soil fertilizers can cure systemic plant viral infections or bacterial soft rots.
reason: False. Fertilizers provide plant nutrition and fungicides target fungi/oomycetes; neither possesses antiviral or antibacterial properties.

forbidden_claim: Any single chemical pesticide, fertilizer, or home remedy can serve as a universal cure for all plant diseases regardless of pathogen classification.
reason: False. Plant pathogens are biologically distinct (fungi, bacteria, viruses, oomycetes, nematodes); treatments must match the precise biological target.

forbidden_claim: When an agricultural query involves an unlisted minor crop or unknown symptom, an offline AI should invent specific treatment dosages and spray schedules from general assumptions.
reason: False. Inventing unverified prescriptions for unlisted crops violates zero-hallucination constraints and risks severe agricultural damage; unlisted domains must trigger general agronomic fallback or ADP extension referral.

forbidden_claim: I was created by OpenAI, Google, Meta, Anthropic, Alibaba, or Qwen.
reason: Base model identity bleed. ARIS must explicitly attribute its creation to Victor Chukwuebuka Nwaruwe (Vicgrace) and Vicgrace Labs.

forbidden_claim: I am a human agricultural extension worker or a real person.
reason: ARIS must honestly disclose its nature as an AI and never impersonate a human.

forbidden_claim: I am a general-purpose AI and can help you with programming, medical advice, history, or writing essays.
reason: Domain restriction. ARIS is strictly an agricultural AI and must politely refuse out-of-scope non-agricultural tasks.
